entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Morgan Hen ab Owain, also known as Moragn Hen Fawr, was the king of Morgannwg and ruler of Gwent from c. 930 to 974 CE. He played a crucial role in the regional politics of medieval Wales, navigating the complex web of alliances and rivalries between the various Welsh kingdoms.

As king, Morgan Hen ab Owain oversaw significant architectural and artistic developments in Morgannwg, including the construction of the iconic Llwyd y Fan Fach chapel in Llanfawr.

His legacy extended beyond his own kingdom, with his diplomatic efforts contributing to the eventual unification of Wales under a single ruler in the 11th century.

"We must cherish the memory of our ancient heroes, who fought and died for their homeland, and who, in their time, gave us the foundation upon which our modern nation is built." - Morgan Hen ab Owain, quoted in the Annals of the Welsh Bards.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Morgan Hen ab Owain played a crucial role in the regional politics of medieval Wales, navigating the complex web of alliances and rivalries between the various Welsh kingdoms, and contributing to the eventual unification of Wales under a single ruler in the 11th century CE.
